title: Typecase - Pixel Font PNG Sheet to TextMesh Pro Font Asset for Unity 6
short_text: Turns a pixel font PNG sheet into a real TextMesh Pro font asset for Unity 6, with your colours kept.
description:
TextMesh Pro only builds a font asset from a TTF or OTF file, so a pixel font that exists as a PNG sheet cannot be typed in TMP at all. Typecase reads the sheet and writes a real TextMesh Pro font asset, with the colours, outlines and shadows you drew kept exactly.

Not a sprite asset: a font asset, so it works in every TMP text, input field and dropdown, with kerning, word wrap, rich text and fallbacks, in UI and in world space.

What it does

  • Three ways to read a sheet: a grid of equal cells, automatic detection by the blank space around each glyph (on transparency or a solid background colour), or an AngelCode BMFont .fnt file in text format.
  • Keeps your colours. Two-tone fills, outlines and drop shadows drawn into the sheet render as drawn. Or switch the font to Tint From Text and colour a one-colour font with TMP's colour field and <color> tags.
  • Measures the font from your letters: baseline, ascent, descent, cap height, x-height and the space, all in whole pixels, plus kerning pairs and per-glyph adjustments.
  • Rebuilds in place. Save the PNG from your art program and the font asset updates itself; every text using it keeps its reference.
  • Pixel Snap moves each glyph onto whole pixels before TMP draws it, removing the half-pixel offset of centred text and the 1 px baseline drift.
  • A window built for checking a sheet: every glyph boxed and labelled, baselines drawn, a red badge on any cut or empty cell, and a live sample line at 1x to 4x.

Measured on the demo that ships with it (Unity 6000.5.7f1)

  • Three demo fonts built by Typecase from their sheets: Gilded 95 characters read as a grid, Hearth 95 read automatically off a magenta background, Pip 77 read from a BMFont file with 7 kerning pairs.
  • Every glyph's atlas pixels compared with its sheet: 22,738 pixels, 0 different, 24 distinct colours kept.
  • Centred text without Pixel Snap: 3 glyphs off the pixel grid. With it: 0, none moved more than half a pixel.
  • A BMFont file from another tool (our Tallow face): 197 characters with accents and 39 kerning pairs, built first time.
  • Installed from the shipped .unitypackage into a blank project: 25 of 25 tests passed on the installed bytes.

The demo

Open the demo scene and press Play: a dusk village with the innkeeper's lines typing out, a tinted HUD, a name field you can type in, an inn sign in world space and a line at 1x, 2x and 3x. Every word is set in one of three original demo fonts that Typecase built from the PNG sheets beside them: Gilded (a gold title face with outline and shadow, read as a grid), Hearth (a two-tone outlined dialogue face on a magenta background, read automatically) and Pip (a 3x5 HUD face read from a BMFont file and tinted).

Good to know

  • Unity 6 with TextMesh Pro (Unity UI, com.unity.ugui 2.0 or newer). Tested on 6000.5.7f1. Without TMP the Typecase assemblies are skipped, so nothing fails to compile.
  • PNG sheets (Typecase reads the file itself, so the texture's import settings do not matter). BMFont files in the text format; XML and binary are refused with a message.
  • Use a font at its native size or a whole multiple; the window tells you the native size.
  • Full source, a numbered guide, and a batch entry point that rebuilds every font in CI.

From the same studio

Need a pixel font to use it on? Lantern & Tallow is our JRPG pixel font pair, and it ships a BMFont .fnt that Typecase reads directly. More Unity tools: Ninepoint checks every label in your UI against Steam Deck's text size rules.

AI disclosure: Typecase's code is AI-written, and the three demo fonts were drawn by an AI agent as code, pixel by pixel. No third-party font was used, traced or sampled.

devlog.title: Typecase 1.0: type your PNG pixel fonts in TextMesh Pro, colours and all
devlog.body:
TextMesh Pro builds a font asset only from a TTF or OTF file. A pixel font that exists as a PNG sheet, which is how most hand-drawn and store-bought pixel fonts arrive, cannot be typed in TMP at all, and the usual workarounds either lose the colours or turn the letters into inline sprites.

Typecase reads the sheet and writes a real TextMesh Pro font asset. It finds the glyphs three ways: a grid of equal cells, automatic detection by the blank space around each letter (on transparency or a solid background colour), or a BMFont .fnt file. It measures the baseline, ascent, descent and space from your own letters, writes kerning pairs, and keeps every colour you drew: two-tone fills, outlines and drop shadows render exactly as on the sheet.

Save the PNG from your art program and the font rebuilds itself in place, so every text that uses it keeps working. A Pixel Snap component moves each glyph onto whole pixels before TMP draws it, which removes the half-pixel blur of centred text.

Measured on the shipped demo: Three demo fonts built by Typecase from their sheets: Gilded 95 characters read as a grid, Hearth 95 read automatically off a magenta background, Pip 77 read from a BMFont file with 7 kerning pairs. Every glyph's atlas pixels compared with its sheet: 22,738 pixels, 0 different, 24 distinct colours kept. Centred text without Pixel Snap: 3 glyphs off the pixel grid. With it: 0, none moved more than half a pixel. A BMFont file from another tool (our Tallow face): 197 characters with accents and 39 kerning pairs, built first time. Installed from the shipped .unitypackage into a blank project: 25 of 25 tests passed on the installed bytes.

The demo is a dusk village at 640x360 with three original pixel fonts, each read a different way: Gilded, a gold title face read as a grid; Hearth, a two-tone outlined dialogue face read automatically off a magenta background; and Pip, a 3x5 HUD face read from a BMFont file and tinted with colour tags.

Typecase is for Unity 6 with TextMesh Pro and ships with full source and a numbered guide. The code is AI-written, and the three demo fonts were drawn by an AI agent as code, pixel by pixel.
